medium: Pencil on a spiral-bound sketchbook page
provenance: Drawn by Larry from memory on 2026-09-05, the day of the photograph-by-photograph sitting. His son photographed the page in the sketchbook the same afternoon (phone photograph, file timestamp 13:31) and sent it to the archive; the sheet stays with the family. He offered to draw the three sheets himself; his son had not raised it. They were looking at photographs together, and after he had explained more than once where one thing stood in relation to another he said it would be easier to draw it. He was not looking at any photograph while drawing. The three sheets were drawn in one sitting in the order photographed, and he wrote each label as he drew the thing it names. He talked as he drew all three; his son listened and did not take notes, so what he said survives only as his son's later summaries, filed as paraphrase recollections and shown below. On 2026-09-12 his son scanned the three sheets flat with a phone, into one three-page PDF (Scan_20260912_124415 dads drawings Vietnam.pdf, 12:44, kept in the archive as it arrived); this sheet is page 3. The image shown is that page, taken out of the PDF without re-encoding and given a quarter turn so the binding is at the top, as the sheet was photographed and is described here. The phone photograph of 2026-09-05 (IMG_20260905_133124.JPG_compressed.JPEG) is kept unchanged. Comparing the two captures, nothing on the sheet was found to have been added or removed in the week between them. The scan also takes in the blank back of the facing page, folded over above the binding.
title: Tu Do Street, Saigon
description: A street map, drawn in pencil on a sketchbook page. A wide band runs from the top of the page to the bottom, a little left of centre, with a column of long narrow shapes drawn inside it and, near the bottom, an arrow pointing down on its left and an arrow pointing up on its right. At the top of the band is a circle containing the letter M. Along the top-left, the words TO BASE /A PORT with a short arrow pointing left beneath them and, lower, a long line running from the left page edge to the band, where it turns down. Along the top-right, TU DO STREET, written above the first of three horizontal lines that cross the right half of the page. A long vertical line runs the full height of the page near its right edge. Between the second and third horizontal lines are three small rectangles above the word FLOWERS and a small star-like mark. Below the third line, a box against the vertical line carries a label that is not transcribed because one letter cannot be read with confidence; a small shape sits beside the right-hand end of the first line. On the left, a box carries a label not transcribed for the same reason. The word SAIGON is written in the lower left. Beside the vertical line, written vertically, is a two-word inscription that is not transcribed because a letter in it cannot be read with confidence. Nothing on the sheet gives scale or compass direction.
researchNotes: This is the itinerary on the Saigon place record drawn as a map, in the same terms he used at the photographs on 2026-09-05: Tu Do, 'a street with all the bars' (VN-0065), the street of flowers parallel to it (VN-0068), the river with the floating restaurant on the far side (VN-0079), and the block where he felt the 30 March 1965 bombing. The circled M at the head of the central band, the star-like mark by FLOWERS, the shape by the first line, and the three inscriptions not transcribed are not interpreted here; what the unread boxes say is his to tell. The flat scan of 2026-09-12 did not settle any of the three: read at full resolution, each still has a letter that cannot be read with confidence, so they stay untranscribed until he reads them. How the pieces sit relative to one another on the sheet is his memory of the city. His son reports that he said the circled M stands for Market and that an explosion went off there; whether he was present was not settled that day (paraphrase recollection of 2026-09-05). On 2026-09-12 he told it in his own words, shown below: he was “probably 6 or 8 bars away from the explosion,” ran toward it, heard someone say in English that it was a bicycle bomb, and tried to stop a woman’s bleeding until a Vietnamese took over. In his telling he was there. Which market and which explosion are still not identified. 2026-09-15, standard public place names (his son's rule, CLAUDE.md "Place names"): title was "“Tu Do Street”, Saigon"; the words as he wrote them remain in labels.
